title: SGD-DyG: Self-Reliant Global Dependency Apprehending on Dynamic Graphs

problem.claim: Learning on dynamic graphs requires capturing global spatial-temporal dependencies.

gap.claim: Existing dynamic-graph learning approaches inadequately capture global spatial-temporal dependency because they capture biased spatial and temporal dependencies, weakening their coupling.

contributions.claim: The paper proposes the Self-Reliant Global Dependency Apprehending Framework on Dynamic Graphs, named SGD-DyG.
A frequency self-enhanced learning module examines global inherent interactions among node features in the frequency domain.
A global-local-mixed self-supervised learning module maximizes spatial-temporal mutual information between local node and global graph embeddings.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report extensive experiments on seven real-world dynamic graph datasets.
The authors report that SGD-DyG consistently exceeds state-of-the-art models.

narrative_sequence.summary: Dynamic graphs are presented as more precise models of real-world applications, motivating research on learning over them.
Existing approaches inadequately capture global spatial-temporal dependency because spatial and temporal dependencies are biased and weakly coupled.
The authors propose the SGD-DyG framework to address this limitation.
The framework combines frequency-domain self-enhanced learning with global-local-mixed self-supervised learning.
The authors report experiments on seven real-world dynamic graph datasets and claim consistent improvement over state-of-the-art models.

source_observation.claim: The proposed approach addresses spatial-temporal dependency modeling through both frequency-domain feature interactions and mutual-information-based local-global learning.

interpretation.claim: Combining complementary dependency views may help address coupling weaknesses between spatial and temporal representations.

application.claim: For dynamic-graph tasks, consider pairing global feature-interaction modeling with objectives that connect local node representations to global graph representations.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this combination is effective beyond the reported dynamic-graph datasets or tasks.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the downstream tasks, dataset names, evaluation metrics, or baseline models.
The abstract does not provide implementation details, quantitative results, or ablation findings.
The abstract does not establish independent verification or reproducibility.
